article_title: Development research on an AI English learning support system to facilitate learner-generated-context-based learning
citation: Donghwa Lee, Hong-hyeon Kim, Seok-Hyun Sung. (2023). Development research on an AI English learning support system to facilitate learner-generated-context-based learning. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-022-10172-2
title: Learner-Generated Context (LGC) framework: learners as creators of their own learning contexts
description: The LGC framework holds that learning is constructed across a continuum of contexts, and that the preferred form is one in which "learners become the creators of their learning contexts and construct knowledge autonomously by interacting with or creating resources (e.g., people, technology, and learning contents) with self-defined learning goals". The article uses LGC to define LGC-based learning and to derive design guidance for digital tools, categorizing facilitation into designing technology for learners' contexts, personalized learning support, and assisting interactions with resources.
requirements: Digital technology must be designed so learners can generate and control their own learning context rather than receive unilaterally imposed contexts
constraints: The framework assumes learners have self-defined learning purposes; the article notes prior LGC studies assumed the presence of human instructors capable of timely feedback
examples: The study applied the framework to design an AI English learning support system for Korean secondary students
key_sources: Donghwa Lee, Hong-hyeon Kim, Seok-Hyun Sung. (2023). Development research on an AI English learning support system to facilitate learner-generated-context-based learning. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-022-10172-2

article_title: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender clinical competence of health professionals in Poland and Spain: results of the health exclusion research in Europe (HERE) study.
citation: Karniej Piotr, Dissen Anthony, Pietrzykowski Łukasz, Juárez-Vela Raúl, Sabater Antonio Martinez, Kulińska Janina, Zieliński Jakub, Czapla Michał. (2025). Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender clinical competence of health professionals in Poland and Spain: results of the health exclusion research in Europe (HERE) study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-025-06744-4
title: LGBT-DOCSS scale (Polish and Spanish versions) as used in the HERE study
description: The LGBT-DOCSS is a validated self-administered instrument for assessing clinical skills in working with LGBT patients, used here in newly validated Polish and Spanish versions. It is an "18-item instrument employs a 7-point Likert scale, with eight items reverse-coded" to score positive attitudes, knowledge and preparedness. Scores yield an overall score plus Clinical Preparedness, Attitudes and Knowledge subscales, with higher scores indicating greater preparedness, more positive attitudes and better knowledge. The Polish version showed a Cronbach's alpha of 0.789 and the Spanish version 0.769.
requirements: Administered as a self-administered questionnaire with Likert responses and eight reverse-coded items to ensure accurate scoring of positive attitudes, knowledge, and preparedness.
constraints: The article notes that the LGBT-DOCSS does not have predetermined norms.
target_learners: health professionals practicing or studying medical professions in Poland and Spain
target_learning_goals: clinical preparedness, attitudes, and knowledge in working with LGBT patients
examples: Used in the HERE study cross-sectional survey of 673 health professionals, with the Spanish version validated for this study and both language versions provided as supplementary materials.
